scope: NativeProcessSession.kt: authenticated process-group teardown, parent-exit cleanup and cancellation races
NativeCancellationTest.kt and ProcessLeaseTest.kt: inspected source only
conclusion: No additional source-proven defect was identified within the assigned scope.

evidence.observation: Group signaling is independent of Process.isAlive. The authenticated UUID/PID/starttime record must be accepted, and ownership is checked using the original leader or a surviving token-bearing group/session member before SIGKILL.

A stopping guard coalesces concurrent termination attempts. The shared gate covers group creation and ownership check/signaling, including destruction of an unpublished bootstrap; main-thread calls dispatch the bounded cleanup to IO.

Cancellation and process registration synchronize on the same lock. A late registration sees sticky cancellation and invokes termination; identity-based detach cannot clear a distinct registered Process.

excluded_documented_limits: Denied /proc identity or environment access, bounded scan/gate-budget exhaustion, and cache eviction can prevent proof and leave helpers; these are documented fail-closed limits in docs/launch/reviews/reviewer-01.json.
The gate coordinates current NativeProcessSession groups rather than unrelated native group creation. No same-UID arbitrary-code compromise is asserted as a new vulnerability.
coverage_gaps: The exited-leader fixture explicitly invokes cancel after detecting leader death; it covers cancel-driven orphan cleanup but does not independently establish bounded normal completion when an inherited output pipe remains open. This is a test-evidence gap, not a proven additional defect.

Existing registration stress coverage uses a fake Process; the source-reviewed native fixtures are not a device stress result for simultaneous main-thread cancellation, IO finalization, and bootstrap publication.
